sources.title: J. S. Milne, Algebraic Groups (corrected 2022 printing, Cambridge University Press)
sources.locator: Ch. 2 §§2.1-2.5, printed pp. 39-41 (PDF 50-52); Ch. 3 §§3(a)-(e), printed pp. 64-68 (PDF 75-79); Ch. 4 §§4(a),(c)-(d), printed pp. 83-88 (PDF 94-99); Conventions and §1.19, printed pp. 3 and 12 (PDF 14 and 23); Appendix A §A(c), printed pp. 574-575 (PDF 585-586). Read in full over these ranges.

contents.name: Ch. 2 §§2.1-2.5: coordinate rings and group laws of G_m and GL_n
Ch. 2 §2.1: the additive group scheme G_a
contents.reason: The additive group is not used by any item of this pair: the split-torus example needs only G_m and the rational-representation example needs only G_m and GL_n.

contents.name: Ch. 3 §3(a), Proposition 3.1: (Spm(A),Spm(Δ)) is an algebraic group iff the induced operation is a group structure on Hom(A,R) for all k-algebras R
Ch. 3 §3(b), Notation 3.2 and display (16): evaluation formulas (Δf)(g1,g2)=f(g1g2), (εf)(g)=f(e), (Sf)(g)=f(g^{-1})
Ch. 3 §3(b), Definition 3.3: commutative Hopf algebra over a commutative ring, finitely generated Hopf algebra
Ch. 3 §3(b), paragraph 3.4: uniqueness of (ε,S) and compatibility of Hopf algebra morphisms with them
contents.reason: The scaffold defines a Hopf algebra morphism to preserve Δ, ε and S explicitly, so this automaticity and uniqueness statement is not consumed by any item; the uniqueness needed for quotients is supplied by the quotient universal property in the Hopf-ideal lemma.

contents.name: Ch. 3 §3(b)-(c), diagrams (17)-(18) and Proposition 3.6: the Hopf diagrams are exactly the reversed group-object diagrams
Ch. 3 §3(c), Corollary 3.7: Spm is an equivalence from finitely generated Hopf algebras to affine algebraic groups with quasi-inverse (G,m) ↦ (O(G),O(m))
Ch. 3 §3(d), Definition 3.8 and Proposition 3.9: Hopf subalgebras and images of Hopf algebra homomorphisms
Ch. 3 §3(d), Definition 3.10 and Proposition 3.11: Hopf ideals and kernels of Hopf algebra homomorphisms
Ch. 3 §3(d), Propositions 3.12-3.14: quotient Hopf structure on A/a, first isomorphism, and surjective-injective factorization
Ch. 3 §3(e), Proposition 3.15: closed subschemes of G correspond to ideals of O(G), algebraic subgroups to Hopf ideals
Ch. 4 §4(a), printed pp. 83-84: linear representations of G, faithfulness, and the equivalence with group actions on Va
Ch. 4 §4(a), Remark 4.1 with (24)-(25): bijection between representations and O(G)-comodules, matrix-coefficient form Δ(a_ij)=Σ_l a_il⊗a_lj, ε(a_ij)=δ_ij
Ch. 4 §4(c), Proposition 4.7: every comodule is a filtered union of finite-dimensional subcomodules
Ch. 4 §4(c), Corollary 4.8: every representation is a filtered union of finite-dimensional subrepresentations
Ch. 4 §4(d), Theorem 4.9: the regular representation has a faithful finite-dimensional subrepresentation
Ch. 4 §4(d), Corollary 4.10 and Remark 4.11: every affine algebraic group is isomorphic to a closed subgroup of GLn, so linear groups are exactly affine groups
Conventions, printed p. 3, and §1.19, printed p. 12: algebraic schemes are of finite type over k and affine algebraic schemes are max-spectra of finitely generated algebras
Appendix A §A(c), A.24 and A.26, printed pp. 574-575: closed subschemes of an affine algebraic scheme are spectra of quotient algebras and quotient maps are immersions

contents.name: September 24th lecture, Lemma 7 (Yoneda anti-equivalence of algebras and representable functors) and Definition 9 (affine group scheme as a representable functor to groups)
September 26th lecture, Definition 14 and Remark 15: commutative Hopf k-algebra with Δ, ε, σ
September 26th lecture, Theorem 19 and Remark 20: antiequivalence between affine group schemes over k and commutative Hopf k-algebras
October 1st lecture, Example 31(2)-(3): GL_n with Δ(x_ij)=Σ_k x_ik⊗x_kj and G_m with Δ(t)=t⊗t
September 29th lecture, Definitions 21-23: cartesian products of representables are represented by tensor products of algebras
September 29th lecture, Definition 25 (group object) and Definition 28 (converting between k[G] and G(R) via Δ, ε, σ)
October 1st lecture, Remark 30: recovering the Hopf algebra structure of k[G] from the group structure by Δ(a)=(ι1 × ι2)(a)
October 1st lecture, Definitions 34-35: closed subschemes defined by quotient ideals, and Hopf ideals
October 1st lecture, Definition 36 and Proposition 37: closed subgroup schemes and the equivalence with Hopf ideals
October 3rd lecture, Remark 40: verification that a Hopf ideal defines a subgroup functor on R-points
October 3rd lecture, Definition 41: kernel of a morphism of affine group schemes
contents.reason: Scheme-theoretic kernels of group morphisms are not used by this pair; the page consumes only kernels of Hopf algebra homomorphisms, which are treated by the Hopf-ideal lemma from Milne.

contents.name: October 22nd lecture, Definitions 103-105 and Remark 104: the three equivalent notions of rational representation and the comodule diagrams
October 22nd lecture, Definition 107: subcomodules, quotient comodules, direct sums and tensor products
October 27th lecture, Remark 106: translations between group functor morphisms, actions and comodule maps
October 27th lecture, Definition 108: regular, trivial and standard representations
October 27th lecture, Lemma 109: for a finite-dimensional comodule with ρ(m_j)=Σ_i m_i⊗a_ij one has Δ(a_ij)=Σ_k a_ik⊗a_kj
October 27th lecture, Definition 110, Theorem 111 and Remark 112: local finiteness — every element lies in a finite-dimensional subcomodule
October 27th lecture, Fact 113: every Hopf algebra is a directed union of finitely generated Hopf subalgebras
contents.reason: Sub-Hopf-algebra approximation is not used by the pair: finite generation enters as the hypothesis on the coordinate ring of a finite-type scheme, and no statement here needs a finitely generated Hopf subalgebra of a non-finitely-generated one.

contents.name: October 27th and 29th lectures, Definition 115 and Theorem 117: algebraic means k[G] finitely generated, and every affine algebraic group scheme is a closed subgroup of GLn
October 29th lecture, Remark 118: closed embedding coincides with surjectivity of the corresponding Hopf algebra map

contents.reason: The B page exhibits the comodule-to-representation dictionary on a split torus; the linearity theorem and its finite-dimensional subcomodule argument are the A page's business and are not reproved in the examples.

contents.name: Ch. 2 §2.1: the additive group scheme G_a
contents.reason: The additive group is not consumed by any B-page example: the torus example uses G_m and the graded-comodule example uses G_m and GL_n only.

October 1st lecture, Example 31(3)-(6): translation of G_m, SL_n, μ_n and G_a(1)
